## FAQs
How long does medical record retrieval take?

Traditional retrieval services typically deliver records in two to six weeks, depending on provider responsiveness, custodian backlogs, and authorization complexity. AI-powered platforms compress this timeline to days through automated follow-up workflows and direct provider integrations.

How much do medical record retrieval companies charge?

Pricing models vary across providers. Per-request fees typically range from $20 to $50, plus pass-through provider fees set under state record-fee schedules. Enterprise providers more commonly use custom or volume-based pricing structures. Firms should compare total cost per case, including provider fees and any value-added services like chronology preparation, rather than the headline retrieval rate alone.

What's the difference between traditional retrieval services and AI-powered platforms?

Traditional services manage the request, follow-up, and delivery process through established provider relationships, returning organized records that firms then process manually. AI-powered platforms extend the workflow further, automating chronology generation and demand letter drafting alongside retrieval.

How long does medical record retrieval take?

Traditional retrieval services typically deliver records in two to six weeks, depending on provider responsiveness, custodian backlogs, and authorization complexity. AI-powered platforms compress this timeline to days through automated follow-up workflows and direct provider integrations. Turnaround for any individual request still depends on the responding facility's internal release-of-information process.

How much do medical record retrieval companies charge?

Pricing models vary across providers. Per-request fees typically range from $20 to $50, plus pass-through provider fees set under state record-fee schedules. Enterprise providers more commonly use custom or volume-based pricing structures. Firms should compare total cost per case, including provider fees and any value-added services like chronology preparation, rather than the headline retrieval rate alone.

What's the difference between traditional retrieval services and AI-powered platforms?

Traditional services manage the request, follow-up, and delivery process through established provider relationships, returning organized records that firms then process manually. AI-powered platforms extend the workflow further, automating chronology generation and demand letter drafting alongside retrieval. The distinction matters most for firms evaluating whether to address only the retrieval bottleneck or the broader case preparation cycle.

How much do AI legal tools cost?

Pricing spans a wide range by category. Case management platforms run roughly $49 to $149 per user monthly, and research or generative AI platforms for large firms often reach $1,000 or more per user monthly under custom enterprise contracts. Contract lifecycle systems commonly land between $30,000 and $150,000 or more annually. Purpose-built case preparation tools frequently use flat-fee or consumption-based pricing, which suits contingency practices scaling case volume without proportional cost.

What is the best free AI legal tool?

No free tool is grounded in verified legal authority, so none is suited to citation-dependent work without verification. General-purpose assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini offer capable free tiers for drafting and summarization, while Perplexity aids preliminary research and NotebookLM organizes uploaded documents.
